subsystems.name: Driver accelerator and production target
subsystems.role: makes antiprotons by smashing a high-energy proton beam into a metal target — most of the energy ends up as heat and other particles, not antiprotons.

subsystems.name: Deceleration and cooling
subsystems.role: antiprotons leave the target fast and scattered; they must be slowed and squeezed in momentum before any trap can hold them.

subsystems.name: Penning traps and storage rings
subsystems.role: a strong magnetic field plus electrostatic wells suspend charged antiprotons in vacuum, away from any matter they would annihilate on.

subsystems.name: Antihydrogen synthesis and neutral traps
subsystems.role: neutral antimatter is easier to store compactly than a charged beam; antiprotons are combined with positrons and held in a magnetic minimum trap.

subsystems.name: Vacuum, cryogenics and shielding
subsystems.role: even a trace of residual gas destroys the product, and annihilations release penetrating gamma rays and pions.

subsystems.name: Power and heat rejection
subsystems.role: production is enormously energy-hungry; a dedicated plant would need a very large continuous power source and a way to dump waste heat.

subsystems.name: Annihilation converter
subsystems.role: turns stored antimatter back into useful thrust or electricity on demand.

buildSteps.title: Build the proton driver
buildSteps.detail: A powerful synchrotron accelerates protons to tens of gigaelectronvolts and delivers them in intense bunches.

buildSteps.title: Make and collect antiprotons
buildSteps.detail: Bunches strike a cooled metal target; a pulsed magnetic lens captures the small fraction of antiprotons produced at wide angles.

buildSteps.title: Cool and decelerate
buildSteps.detail: Rings and cooling systems reduce the beam's momentum spread by orders of magnitude so it can be captured.

buildSteps.title: Stack in traps
buildSteps.detail: Antiprotons are captured in Penning traps and accumulated over many machine cycles, since each fill yields only a minuscule population.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise antihydrogen
buildSteps.detail: Slow antiprotons are mixed with accumulated positrons so they combine into neutral antihydrogen atoms, which can then be held in a magnetic trap.

buildSteps.title: Load transportable storage
buildSteps.detail: For propulsion use the product must be moved: portable cryogenic traps or antihydrogen traps would be charged and shipped to the point of use.

buildSteps.title: Scale the power supply
buildSteps.detail: A dedicated production ring placed in close solar orbit would use very large arrays to supply continuous power far beyond any ground facility.

buildSteps.title: Recover energy or thrust
buildSteps.detail: Annihilation products are absorbed in a blanket or directed through a magnetic nozzle, converting mass directly into heat, electricity or exhaust velocity.

prerequisites.why: accelerator laboratories have made and trapped antiprotons since the 1980s, but only in tiny numbers.
neutral antihydrogen has been produced and trapped since 2010, proving the storage principle at laboratory scale.
antimatter must never touch ordinary matter, so storage relies on technology already used in accelerators and surface science.
only a minute fraction of the driver beam becomes trapped antiprotons; scale-up needs gains of many orders of magnitude.
a gram of antiprotons is about 6×10²³ particles — traps today hold populations inconceivably smaller than that.

prerequisites.tech: Very large off-world power and heat rejection
prerequisites.why: the energy cost of production always exceeds what can be recovered, so a plant must run on surplus power, not on its own output.

pathway.milestone: microscopic antiproton and antihydrogen samples at dedicated decelerator facilities, used for precision physics
pathway.unlocks: measurement of antimatter's properties and the basic trapping techniques.

pathway.milestone: dedicated higher-power production ring with stacking, lifting output by orders of magnitude
pathway.unlocks: quantities large enough to test storage, transport and annihilation conversion, not just study single atoms.

pathway.milestone: portable traps and first in-space experiments, using antimatter as an ignition catalyst for fission or fusion rather than as bulk fuel
pathway.unlocks: a near-term propulsion role that needs far less antimatter than pure antimatter drive.

pathway.milestone: solar-orbit production ring feeding a delivery network
pathway.unlocks: stored antimatter as a compact propellant and energy buffer for deep-space missions.
high specific-impulse transport and extremely dense energy storage — with the caveat that net energy return stays negative.
